text: This is a Flagsmith feature flag... evaluated inside Postgres. No SDK. No network call. Just SQL.

Your app reads flags through Flagsmith's SDK. But so much of your product lives in the database: search ranking, row-level security, nightly jobs, reports. None of it can see your flags. And every flip goes live for everyone, with no review step.

P G smith keeps a live replica of your Flagsmith environments inside Postgres, compiled into plain SQL. Flip a flag in Flagsmith... and Postgres has it in under a second. No extra service: the database syncs itself.
A Flagsmith experiment takes four steps. Let's run all four, from SQL.

Step one: a multivariate flag. Search ranking: control, or boosted by thirty-day sales, split fifty-fifty. In Postgres, one function call picks the arm, and the same query ranks with it. Two users. Two rankings. One query.
Step two: pick the metrics. Clicks and add to cart, with search latency as a guardrail, recorded straight from SQL.

Step three: split the traffic. Postgres queues the exposures and ships them to Flagsmith. Bucketing matches the SDK exactly: ten thousand identities, zero mismatches. Simulated traffic, real statistics: boosted lifts clicks twenty-three percent, add to cart sixty-four. Latency stays flat.
Step four: ship the winner. Complete the experiment in Flagsmith, roll out boosted to everyone, and the SQL never changes.

A release is rarely one flag: ours also promotes a new checkout from staging. Flag Shift, a terraform plan for flags, runs both configurations over all hundred thousand users, and catches this: four thousand four hundred twenty-six enterprise accounts would lose their checkout.
And a twist: the same twenty-five percent rollout in staging and production picks different people. Only a quarter overlap. Flag Shift re-keys the plan, so it's exact.
Fix the order, and apply. Flagsmith updates, Postgres syncs, and a re-plan proves nothing else moved. And if Flagsmith goes down, Postgres keeps serving the last good configuration.

Same answers as Flagsmith? It passes all two hundred thirty of Flagsmith's engine tests, and matches the official engine on five thousand random configurations. And it's fast: a million users times fifty flags, in six seconds.
P G smith. Pure SQL, for Supabase, R D S, and any Postgres. Flagsmith flags, where your data lives.
